input.summary:
Implemented a complete in-memory Task Management API in TypeScript with Node.js built-ins only. The system comprises:

**Files written (9 source files + tsconfig):**

- `src/types.ts` — All domain models (User, Project, Task, Comment, Notification), typed event payloads (TaskAssigned, TaskStatusChanged, CommentAdded, MemberAdded, TaskCreated), and HTTP helper types.

- `src/event-bus.ts` — Generic typed EventBus with `publish<K>(event, payload)` and `subscribe<K>(event, callback)`. Fully type-safe via the EventMap interface; no service directly imports another service.

- `src/user-service.ts` — Full CRUD for users, duplicate-email guard, in-memory Map storage.

- `src/project-service.ts` — Full CRUD for projects, `addMember`/`removeMember` with validation, publishes `member.added` events via EventBus.

- `src/task-service.ts` — Full CRUD for tasks, enforced forward-only status transitions (`todo→in-progress→done`), assignment; publishes `task.created`, `task.assigned`, `task.statusChanged` events.

- `src/comment-service.ts` — Create/read/delete comments (with cascade delete by task), publishes `comment.added` events carrying task context supplied by the router.

- `src/notification-service.ts` — Subscribes to all four event types in its constructor and creates per-user notifications. Supports `getNotificationsForUser`, `getAllNotifications`, and `markAsRead`.

- `src/router.ts` — Pure HTTP routing layer using Node's `http` module. Custom `matchRoute()` pattern matcher handles `:param` segments. Parses JSON bodies for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE. Orchestrates cross-service lookups (e.g. fetches task details before creating a comment so the event payload is complete). Routes: GET/POST /users, GET/PUT/DELETE /users/:id, GET/POST /projects, GET/PUT/DELETE /projects/:id, POST/DELETE /projects/:id/members, GET/POST /tasks (with ?projectId filter), GET/PUT/DELETE /tasks/:id, PUT /tasks/:id/status, PUT /tasks/:id/assign, GET/POST /comments (with ?taskId filter), GET/DELETE /comments/:id, GET /notifications (with ?userId filter), PUT /notifications/:id/read.

- `src/main.ts` — Wires all services together, starts the HTTP server on port 3000.

- `src/demo.ts` — Self-contained demo server (port 3001) that exercises all 10 feature areas via real HTTP requests: user CRUD, project CRUD, member add/remove, task creation, assignment, status transitions, comments, notifications (including read marking), update/delete, and error cases. Compiles with zero TypeScript errors and runs end-to-end successfully.
